category_title: At-risk middle school students demonstrating high engagement and professional presentation skills in STEM
minimal_context: The student is assembling a weather box with a radio and flashlight and preparing to present extreme weather safety instructions to the class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are studying extreme weather. I need you to assemble your weather boxes with the weather radio and flashlight, and write down the instructions for finding safe places. You will present this to me and your classmates at the end of the period.

STUDENT: Why are we just presenting to you and the class again? I'm not genuinely excited about science when we just do the same thing every day.

TUTOR: That is the assignment for today. Please start working on your instructions.

STUDENT: (Turns the flashlight on and off, shining it at the wall instead of writing) This is boring. I don't see the point of making these boxes.

TUTOR: You need to stay on task and finish the weather box.

STUDENT: I'm not doing it. You can just give me a referral to the office for discipline because I'm not presenting this to the class.

options.A: Provide specific feedback and guiding questions that force the student to link their safety instructions back to physical evidence.
options.B: Push the student to justify an appropriate media choice for presenting their extreme weather safety instructions to the class.
options.C: Provide an authentic audience for the presentation, such as students from neighboring schools, college students, and adults.
options.D: Step in to revoice the student's ideas about the weather box and position the other classmates as evaluators of their claims.
